name: Create Order
overview: Hmm... ALRIGHT! So, we're on the Order form now. An Order is basically how we keep track of linen pickups and deliveries for a customer. Think of it as the plan that tells us what needs to go out, what needs to come back, and when all of that should happen! Alright... let's create one together!

fields.label: Order Reference ID
fields.explanation: Okay... first up is Order Reference ID. This is just a unique name or number for the order. You can enter your own reference if your team follows a specific format. And if you don't want to worry about it... that's completely fine too. The system can generate one automatically when you save!
fields.tips: Use a consistent naming pattern like ORD-YYYY-NNN so your team can quickly identify orders.

commonQuestions.question: What happens if I leave this blank?
commonQuestions.answer: The system will auto-generate a reference ID when you save the order.

commonQuestions.question: Can I use any format?
commonQuestions.answer: Yes, you can use any format. But a consistent pattern like ORD-YYYY-NNN makes orders easier to find.

fields.label: Customer
fields.explanation: Moving on... let's choose the Customer. This is the customer we're creating the order for. Just start typing the name and the system will help you find the right one. If you can't find a customer here... they're usually inactive or haven't been created yet!
fields.tips: If a customer doesn't show up, check if they are marked as active in the Customers section.

commonQuestions.question: Why can't I find my customer?
commonQuestions.answer: Only active customers appear in the search. Check the Customers page to make sure the customer is active and not deactivated.

commonQuestions.question: Can I create a new customer from here?
commonQuestions.answer: No, you need to create the customer first from the Customers page, then come back to create the order.

fields.label: Order Date
fields.explanation: Next, we have Order Date. This is simply the date on which the order is being created. Most of the time, today's date is EXACTLY what you need, so you can leave it as is. But if you're entering an older order... you can change it here.
fields.tips: If you set this to a past date, the pickup and delivery dates will shift accordingly. This is useful for backdating orders.

commonQuestions.question: Can I set a past date?
commonQuestions.answer: Yes, you can set a past order date. The pickup and delivery dates will adjust to maintain the same number of days between them.

fields.label: Order Type
fields.explanation: Now this one is EXTREMELY important... Order Type. This tells the system what kind of work we're doing. Leasing is the most common option. Rental is usually for short-term usage, and Washing is when the customer sends their own linen to be cleaned. Depending on what you choose here... you'll notice some fields appear or disappear further down the form.
fields.tips: Most orders in this system are Leasing orders. Only choose Rental or Washing if your business specifically uses those workflows.

commonQuestions.question: What is the difference between Leasing and Rental?
commonQuestions.answer: Leasing is for long-term linen contracts where items are delivered and picked up on a schedule. Rental is short-term, like an event or a one-time use.

commonQuestions.question: What does Washing mean?
commonQuestions.answer: A Washing order is when the customer sends their own linen to your facility for cleaning. You pick it up, wash it, and deliver it back.

fields.label: Adjustment Order
fields.explanation: You'll also see Adjustment Order. In most cases, you can leave this turned OFF. This is only used when you're correcting or updating an existing order instead of creating a completely new one.
fields.tips: Only use this when correcting a previous order. New orders should have this turned off.

commonQuestions.question: When should I use Adjustment Order?
commonQuestions.answer: Use it when you need to correct or modify an existing order, like adding items that were missed or adjusting quantities.

fields.label: Delivery Type
fields.explanation: Now, let's figure out how the movement of items will happen. Do we ONLY need to deliver items? ONLY pick them up? Or do BOTH in the same visit?? Most leasing customers usually use Both, because fresh linen is delivered while used linen is collected at the same time.
fields.tips: Most Leasing orders use 'Both' because you deliver fresh linen and pick up the used ones in the same trip.

commonQuestions.question: What if I only need to pick up items?
commonQuestions.answer: Choose 'Pickup' and the system will only show pickup-related fields and items.

fields.label: Pickup Date
fields.explanation: Now for the Pickup Date. This is when your team will go to collect the used linen. It usually defaults to tomorrow, but you can change it as needed. Just be careful not to schedule it on a weekend unless your team is working.
fields.tips: Make sure pickup dates don't fall on weekends or holidays unless your team operates on those days.

commonQuestions.question: Can the pickup date be before the order date?
commonQuestions.answer: Technically yes, but it's unusual. The system allows it for edge cases like backdating.

fields.label: Delivery Date
fields.explanation: And the Delivery Date. This is when you'll drop off the fresh linen. Again, it usually defaults to tomorrow. Just make sure your warehouse has enough time to prepare everything by this date.
fields.tips: Delivery dates should account for processing time. Make sure your warehouse has enough stock to fulfill the order by this date.

commonQuestions.question: What if delivery is delayed?
commonQuestions.answer: You can edit the order later to change the delivery date. The system does not automatically reschedule.

subForms.name: Delivery Item

autoPopulatedTrigger.description: Products auto-populate based on the customer's reserved products after selection

fallbackManual.description: Click this if no products auto-populate for the selected customer

subForms.explanationForMultiple: You can add multiple items to a single order. Let me add a second one to show you.
subForms.explanation: Finally, let's add the actual items to be delivered to the customer! These are the linen products they will receive.

fields.label: Product
fields.explanation: What product are we delivering? For leasing customers, this list only shows items reserved in their agreement. The system often fills this in automatically.

fields.label: Quantity
fields.explanation: How many of these do they need for this delivery cycle? Just enter the number here.

fields.label: Remarks
fields.explanation: Any special notes for this item? Maybe something like 'handle with care' or 'premium quality requested'.

subForms.name: Pickup Item

copyFrom.checkboxLabel: Use same items and quantities as Delivery

subForms.explanationForMultiple: Let me add a second pickup item to show you.
subForms.explanation: These are the items being picked up from the customer. You can add them manually, or use the 'Use same items as Delivery' checkbox to copy the delivery items automatically.

fields.label: Product
fields.explanation: Which product are we picking up? Usually, this is the exact same type of item we delivered to them previously.

fields.label: Quantity
fields.explanation: And how many are we collecting? This might be different from the delivery amount if they're still using some of the items.

fields.label: Remarks
fields.explanation: Need to add any notes? Like 'customer reported 5 damaged items' or anything else the team should know.

subForms.name: Rental Item
subForms.explanation: Now let's add the items being rented out. Just select the item, enter the quantity, and specify how long the customer will keep it.

fields.label: Product
fields.explanation: What product is being rented out?

fields.label: Rental Duration (days)
fields.explanation: How long are they renting this for? Enter the duration in days.

subForms.name: Washing Item
subForms.explanation: For Washing orders, this section is used to capture the items the customer wants cleaned. Simply choose the product and enter the quantity being sent for washing.

fields.label: Product
fields.explanation: Which product did they send to be washed?

fields.label: Quantity
fields.explanation: How many of these items did they send?

wrapUp: Perfect... that's everything you need to create an Order. We've selected a customer, chosen the order type, set the required dates, and added the necessary items. This was only a walkthrough, so no actual data has been saved. Whenever you're ready, you can create a real order! And if you'd like help with another form... just let me know and we'll go through that one as well.
